correctness.rationale: After translation/reflection the support is \(\{0,\ldots,N-1\}\) with decreasing masses. Log-concavity makes successive positive ratios nonincreasing. For \(N=4\) and \(N=5\), monotonicity bounds the mean by \(3/2\) and \(2\) respectively; outside the first mean cell the modal mass itself is adjacent to the mean. In the only nontrivial cell, the conditions \(\mathbb E X\ge1\) become \(ab(1+2c)\ge1\) and \(ab(1+2c+3cd)\ge1\). Bounding every later ratio by \(a\) yields the sharp one-variable polynomial inequalities. Strict monotonicity of those polynomials and equality in every ratio comparison gives the complete equality classification. \(N=2,3\) are covered separately, and reflection covers increasing laws. No finite experiment is used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The quantity is the exact finite-support refinement of a published sharp mean-versus-mode inequality. Supports of size four and five are the first nontrivial cases: sizes two and three force the modal mass to be adjacent to the mean, while size five is the last support size for which monotonicity forces the mean not to pass \(2\). At size six a second interior mean cell becomes possible. Thus the cutoff is structural rather than arbitrary, and the theorem supplies exact sharp constants plus rigidity for the complete pre-transition regime.
